title: The canonical Roos, strict-limit and intrinsic Koszul units agree
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ use the small pro-etale site, the completed ring sheaf $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/t^n)_W$, the constant quotient sheaves $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$ and the unbounded derived category $D(R_W)$ of sheaves of $R_W$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All quotient modules are restricted to $R_W$ along the specified limit projections. Let $W$ be any scheme and $K\in D(R_W)$. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, set $U_n=P\otimes_{R_W}S_{W,n}$ and $V_n=P\otimes_{R_W}[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$, with quotient transitions on $U$ and $(t,1)$ on the two-term factors of $V$. Write $\mathsf C(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod Z_n\to\prod Z_n)[-1]$ for the strict Roos model, with coordinates $(y,x)$ and differential $(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Let $\eta_U:K\to\mathsf C(U)$ and $\eta_V:K\to\mathsf C(V)$ be induced by the strict quotient and degree-zero Koszul augmentations with zero shifted-product component. Let $F(P)$ and $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}:K\to F(P)$ be the explicit intrinsic Koszul fiber and its unit [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. The coordinate map $j_P:F(P)\to\mathsf C(V)$, $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$, is a chain isomorphism sending $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}$ to $\eta_V$. If $a:V\to U$ is induced by the quotient augmentations and $\rho$ is the normalized strict Roos comparison, the natural isomorphism
$$d_K=\rho_U\circ\mathsf C(a)\circ j_P:F(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim U$$
satisfies $d_K\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}=\rho_U\eta_U=\operatorname{comp}_K$, where $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is the canonical derived strict quotient-augmentation map. These identifications descend independently of $P$. If $K$ is derived complete in the prescribed Roos-triangle sense [def-weil-derived-complete], then $\eta_U$, $\operatorname{comp}_K$ and the actual intrinsic unit $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}$ are isomorphisms. No boundedness, constructibility or finiteness condition on $W$ is assumed. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, $K[r]$ is again Roos-triangle derived complete whenever $K$ is, and the same conclusions apply to its shifted representative $P[r]$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement] with the given $A,t,W,P$. It verifies the adic-datum hypotheses for $(A,(t))$, identifies the specified quotient projection with $R_W/t^nR_W$, and gives the strict tower map $a:V\to U$ as a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. In particular the principal Koszul tower here is the one in the intrinsic definition, with precisely the transitions $(t,1)$. Countable products of $R_W$-module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so the hypotheses of the strict Roos comparison hold on this site. Work in a common universe in which the small pro-etale site and its module sheaves have the sizes required there.

proof.text: Put $B=\prod_n V_n$ and $f=1-s$. The intrinsic definition gives $F(P)^i=B^i\oplus B^{i-1}$ and $d_F(x,y)=(dx,fx-dy)$; the strict model gives $\mathsf C(V)^i=B^{i-1}\oplus B^i$ and $d_{\mathsf C}(y,x)=(-dy-fx,dx)$. Consequently $d_{\mathsf C}j_P(x,y)=(dy-fx,dx)=j_Pd_F(x,y)$. The inverse is $(y,x)\mapsto(x,-y)$. This proves the chain isomorphism, including its sign, directly. Writing $u_V:P\to B$ for the product of the degree-zero Koszul units, the intrinsic unit is $p\mapsto(u_Vp,0)$, so $j_P$ carries it to $(0,u_Vp)$, exactly $\eta_V$. The coordinate formulas also commute with every chain map $P\to P\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; explicit signed cone and strict augmentation refinement written by Q67

proof.text: Let $u_{U,n}:P\to U_n$ be the quotient tensor unit and $u_{V,n}:P\to V_n$ the degree-zero Koszul tensor unit. On the two-term Koszul factor, the composite of the degree-zero inclusion $R_W[0]\to Q_{W,n}$ and $\epsilon_n:Q_{W,n}\to S_{W,n}[0]$ is the specified quotient $R_W\to S_{W,n}$. Tensoring this equality gives $a_nu_{V,n}=u_{U,n}$. The source transition fixes the degree-zero unit and the quotient transitions compose with the quotient units, so these families are strictly compatible, and $fu_U=fu_V=0$ in the respective products. The strict Roos map is the product of $a_n$ in both coordinates. Thus $\mathsf C(a)\eta_V=(0,(a_nu_{V,n})_n)=(0,(u_{U,n})_n)=\eta_U$ as chain maps, with no choice of a homotopy.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; explicit signed cone and strict augmentation refinement written by Q67

proof.text: The strict Roos functor of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] descends to $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R_W)))$. Since $a$ is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism, it becomes an isomorphism there, and therefore $\mathsf C(a)$ is an isomorphism after localization. Compose it with the chain isomorphism $j_P$ and the normalized comparison $\rho_U$ to obtain the asserted isomorphism $d_K=\rho_U\mathsf C(a)j_P$. The chain equalities in steps 2 and 3 give $d_K\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}=\rho_U\eta_U$. The strict-augmentation clause of the same comparison identifies $\rho_U\eta_U$ with the canonical derived strict quotient-augmentation map $\operatorname{comp}_K$. This uses that clause of its statement, not merely agreement after the tower projections.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; explicit signed cone and strict augmentation refinement written by Q67

proof.text: At $L=E$, [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] supplies the functorial quotient Roos model on flat-term K-flat representatives and its independence of those representatives. The intrinsic definition supplies the localized intrinsic fiber and its specified unit. All maps used above are natural already before localization: a chain map on $P$ is tensored with the identities of the quotient and Koszul factors, its product maps are diagonal in both cone coordinates, and $(-y,x)$ commutes with those diagonal maps. The comparison $\rho$ is natural and independent of its injective resolution. The natural-transformation clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends these transformations and their composite equations; clause (3) identifies transformations agreeing on representatives. The inverse of $j_P$ descends by the same clause. Hence the isomorphism $d_K$ and both unit identities are independent of $P$, and natural in $K$; no functorial choice of an individual resolution is required.

proof.text: Now suppose $K$ is complete in the Roos-triangle convention. Apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to the identity coefficient extension $E\subset E$, with the same uniformizer on both sides and with $Y=W$. Its statement covers arbitrary schemes and unbounded $K$. After the multiplication identification $P\otimes_{R_W}R_W\cong P$, its specified map $\chi_{E/E,K}$ is exactly $\eta_U$: its product coordinates are the actual quotient tensor units and its shifted-product coordinate is zero. That theorem says this specified map is an isomorphism, rather than merely giving some isomorphism to a limit. Thus $\eta_U$ is invertible. The isomorphisms $\rho_U$ and $d_K$ and the equality in step 4 imply that $\operatorname{comp}_K$ and the actual intrinsic unit $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}$ are invertible as well.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; identity-extension specialization of the existing finite-free completed scalar comparison

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$, shifting a flat-term K-flat representative gives another such representative: the terms are reindexed and tensoring with $P[r]$ is, by the signed total-tensor identification, a shift of tensoring with $P$, so acyclicity is preserved. Since the quotient sheaves lie in degree zero, the quotient tower of $P[r]$ is $U[r]$, and its quotient units are the shifts of those of $P$. In the specified cone coordinates the natural chain isomorphism $\sigma_r:\mathsf C(U[r])\to\mathsf C(U)[r]$ is $(y,x)\mapsto((-1)^r y,x)$. Substituting $d_{U[r]}=(-1)^rd_U$ in the differential of the strict model verifies the chain equation; the inverse has the same signs. In particular $\sigma_r\eta_{U[r]}=\eta_U[r]$. Thus $\eta_{U[r]}$ is invertible by step 6. The standard distinguished cone triangle for $1-s$ has first term $\mathsf C(U[r])$ and first map its unshifted product projection. Transport that triangle through $\eta_{U[r]}$; its second map remains $1-s$, and its first map has the components $u_{U[r],n}$. By [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], computed with the K-flat resolution $P[r]\to K[r]$, these components represent exactly the maps $c_n:K[r]\to K[r]_n$ and the termwise product with $1-s$ represents the transition endomorphism of the reduction tower of $K[r]$; by [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined] the system and the $c_n$ computed from any other K-flat resolution are isomorphic to these compatibly with the maps from $K[r]$, so the triangle transports to one for every choice. By [def-weil-derived-complete], this is a completeness triangle for $K[r]$. Applying steps 1--6 to $P[r]$ proves every asserted conclusion for the shift.
